ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Ski jumping is a sport for the brave, conducted on specially constructed jumps that follow the natural slope of the mountain. Athletes wear specialized skis and, without using ski poles, gain high speed on the inrun before launching horizontally into the air, flying a certain distance before landing. It is known that the athlete launches horizontally from point $A$ at the top of the slope with a velocity of $v_{0}=20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and lands at point $B$ on the slope, as shown in the figure. The slope has an inclination angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ and can be considered as an inclined plane. ($g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$)

1. The time $t$ that the athlete is in the air
2. The distance between A and B is $s$.

Athletes wear specialized skis and, without using ski poles, gain high speed on the inrun before launching horizontally into the air, flying a certain distance before landing. The slope has an inclination angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ and can be considered as an inclined plane. ($g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos 37^{\circ}=0.8$) Find: 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point A is located at the upper right of the inclined plane, and point B is located at the lower left of the inclined plane; the angle of inclination of the inclined plane relative to the horizontal line is marked as 37°. The athlete is thrown horizontally to the left from point A, the initial velocity is marked as v0, the dashed line represents the parabolic trajectory from A to B, and point B is on the same inclined straight line. Reasoning: According to the method given in the problem, take the horizontal leftward displacement from A to B as x and the vertical downward displacement as y. Since the initial velocity is horizontal, the projectile motion satisfies x=v0 t, y=1/2 gt^2. Also because B is on the straight inclined plane passing through A, the displacement direction is along the inclined plane, so y/x=tanθ=sin37°/cos37°=0.6/0.8=0.75. Substitute v0=20 m/s and g=10 m/s^2: (1/2 gt^2)/(v0 t)=0.75, that is, (5t^2)/(20t)=0.75, so t/4=0.75, solving gives t=3 s. The distance AB along the inclined plane has length s, and the horizontal component x=s cosθ, so s=x/cosθ=v0 t/cos37°=20×3/0.8=75 m.
